stem: Match each French region to its signature grape.
explanation: Beaujolais: Gamay. Northern Rhône reds: Syrah only. Vallée de la Marne: Pinot Meunier. Madiran: Tannat. Sancerre: Sauvignon Blanc.

stem: Match each Bordeaux appellation to its leading grape.
explanation: Left bank (Saint-Estèphe, Pauillac, Saint-Julien, Margaux) is Cabernet Sauvignon country. Right bank (Saint-Émilion, Pomerol) is Merlot on limestone and clay. Sauternes is botrytised Sémillon with Sauvignon Blanc. Two items can share a grape.

stem: Match each Loire appellation to its grape.
explanation: Central Loire (Sancerre, Pouilly-Fumé): Sauvignon Blanc. Anjou-Saumur (Savennières) and Touraine (Vouvray): Chenin Blanc. Touraine reds (Chinon, Bourgueil): Cabernet Franc. Pays Nantais: Muscadet.

stem: Match each Bourgogne appellation to its grape.
explanation: Chablis is 100% Chardonnay; Meursault is oaked Côte de Beaune Chardonnay; Gevrey-Chambertin is Côte de Nuits Pinot Noir; Bouzeron is the birthplace of Aligoté; Beaujolais Nouveau is Gamay by carbonic maceration.

stem: Match each Rhône appellation to its grape.
explanation: Northern Rhône reds are Syrah only (Côte-Rôtie, Hermitage, Crozes-Hermitage). Condrieu and Château-Grillet are white, mainly Viognier.

stem: Match each grape to the French region most identified with it.
explanation: Gewürztraminer: Alsace. Pinot Meunier: Champagne (Vallée de la Marne). Mourvèdre: Bandol's long-lived rosé. Sciacarello: AOC Ajaccio on Corsica. Tannat: Madiran.

stem: Match each Champagne zone to the grape it is mainly planted with.
explanation: Côte des Blancs (and Côte de Sézanne): Chardonnay on chalk. Montagne de Reims and Côte des Bar: Pinot Noir. Vallée de la Marne: Pinot Meunier, late to bud and early to ripen.

stem: Match each French region to the grapes it is built on.
explanation: Bordeaux blend: the two Cabernets and Merlot. Champagne: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Pinot Meunier. Bourgogne: Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Gamay. Southern Rhône/GSM: Grenache, Syrah, Mourvèdre. Alsace and Loire are the spare whites.

stem: Match each southern or outlying French appellation to its grape.
explanation: Cahors: Malbec (local name Auxerrois). Bandol: Mourvèdre rosé. Ajaccio: Sciacarello. Madiran: Tannat. Corsica's whites are Vermentino; Côtes de Provence rosé is mainly Cinsaut and Grenache.

stem: Which grape is Sancerre made from? (two words)
explanation: Sauvignon Blanc — Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé are the Central Loire's Sauvignon Blancs.

stem: Which grape is Chablis made from?
explanation: 100% Chardonnay.

stem: Which red grape is Beaujolais made from?
explanation: Gamay, often by carbonic maceration.

stem: Which grape is the only red grape allowed in Northern Rhône reds such as Côte-Rôtie and Hermitage?
explanation: Syrah.

stem: Which white grape is Condrieu mainly made from?
explanation: Viognier — peach, pear, rose.

stem: Which grape is Vouvray made from? (two words)
explanation: Chenin Blanc, in sec, demi-sec, moelleux and sparkling styles.

stem: Which red grape makes Madiran's highly tannic wine?
explanation: Tannat.

stem: Which grape is the main one in Vallée de la Marne Champagne? (two words)
explanation: Pinot Meunier — buds late and ripens early, so it copes with cold.

stem: Which grape leads the wines of Pomerol and Saint-Émilion?
explanation: Merlot, on the right bank's limestone and clay.

stem: Which grape is Cahors made from? (its local name is Auxerrois)
explanation: Malbec.

stem: A wine is labelled AOC Pouilly-Fumé. Which region and grape is it?
explanation: Pouilly-Fumé is Central Loire Sauvignon Blanc, with flint/mineral notes. Don't confuse it with Pouilly-Fuissé, Mâconnais Chardonnay.

stem: A wine is labelled AOC Pouilly-Fuissé. Which region and grape is it?
explanation: Pouilly-Fuissé is the Mâconnais's most famous zone: Chardonnay on limestone, more concentrated than Côte de Beaune. Pouilly-Fumé is the Loire Sauvignon Blanc.

stem: In which region are Côte de Nuits and Côte de Beaune?
explanation: Together they form the Côte d'Or, between Dijon and Chagny.

stem: Which zone is the world's most important for Pinot Noir red wine?
explanation: Côte de Nuits (Gevrey-Chambertin, Morey-St-Denis, Chambolle-Musigny). Côte de Beaune is famous for white Chardonnay (Meursault, Montrachet).

stem: Which Bordeaux soil sits on the Garonne bank and suits Cabernet Sauvignon?
explanation: Gravel on the Garonne (left bank); limestone on the Dordogne side. Pauillac's gravel makes the most 'masculine' Cabernet.

stem: Which left-bank appellation's clay gives a soft, 'feminine' Cabernet Sauvignon?
explanation: Margaux (clay). Pauillac is gravel and masculine; Saint-Julien is milder; Saint-Estèphe has limestone and more Merlot.

stem: Which two rivers divide Bordeaux into its three major zones?
explanation: Garonne and Dordogne (which meet in the Gironde).

stem: Which producer received *Premier cru supérieur* in the 1855 Sauternes classification?
explanation: Only d'Yquem; 11 others got Premier cru. Latour and Margaux are among the five red Premiers crus; Ausone is Saint-Émilion.

stem: Which château is *not* one of the five red Premiers crus of the 1855 classification?
explanation: The five: Haut-Brion, Lafite-Rothschild, Latour, Margaux, Mouton Rothschild. Cheval Blanc is Saint-Émilion Premier grand cru classé A.

stem: Which AOC lets producers blend up to 13 grape varieties?
explanation: Châteauneuf-du-Pape, the Southern Rhône's most famous zone. Côte-Rôtie and Hermitage are single-grape Syrah.

stem: Which region is France's main source of rosé?
explanation: Provence, from Syrah, Grenache, Mourvèdre and Cabernet Sauvignon; Côtes de Provence rosé is mainly Cinsaut and Grenache.

stem: Which grape makes the white wines of Corsica?
explanation: Vermentino. Corsica's reds use southern French grapes; Ajaccio uses the native Sciacarello.

stem: Which three white grapes are the most important in the Southern Rhône?
explanation: Viognier/Marsanne/Roussanne in the Rhône. The others are Alsace, Loire and Bourgogne sets.

stem: In the Loire, Cabernet Franc is used at 100% to give a bright, fruity red.
explanation: Touraine (Chinon, Bourgueil) is the Loire's best red zone.

stem: Côte de Beaune is the Bourgogne zone most famous for Pinot Noir; Côte de Nuits is famous for white Chardonnay.
explanation: Reversed: Côte de Nuits is the Pinot Noir heartland; Côte de Beaune is famous for Chardonnay whites (Meursault, Puligny- and Chassagne-Montrachet).

stem: Northern Rhône reds are made from Syrah alone, while Southern Rhône reds are blends led by Grenache.
explanation: North: Syrah only (continental). South: Grenache, Syrah, Cinsaut, Carignan, Mourvèdre (Mediterranean).

stem: The Northern Rhône has a Mediterranean climate suited to Grenache and Mourvèdre.
explanation: That's the South. The North is continental — very hot summers, cold winters — suited to Syrah.

stem: Alsace AOC wines include Gewürztraminer, Muscat Blanc, Riesling, Sylvaner and Pinot Gris.
explanation: Alsace is France's cool-climate white region.

stem: Champagne is made by re-fermentation in the bottle, the Méthode Traditionnelle.
explanation: Champagne's soil is mixed with chalk; the climate is cool and windy.

stem: Champagne was first created by Dom Pérignon, a monk at Hautvillers Abbey.
explanation: The founding story on the slide.

stem: In Bordeaux, Sauvignon Blanc is often blended with Sémillon, for both dry whites and dessert wines.
explanation: Sauternes and Barsac are botrytised Sémillon and Sauvignon Blanc.

stem: Grand Cru Chablis accounts for about half of all Chablis produced.
explanation: Only about 3%. Chablis levels: Petit Chablis, Chablis, Premier Cru, Grand Cru.

stem: Sancerre tends to have more body and fruit, while Pouilly-Fumé shows more mineral, flinty notes.
explanation: Both Sauvignon Blanc and best drunk young.

stem: In 1930 France set up the AOC system to control wine quality across the country.
explanation: Following the phylloxera and economic crises.

stem: The 1855 Bordeaux classification ranked 60 producers from Médoc and Graves into three levels.
explanation: Five levels, Premier cru to Cinquième cru.

stem: Pomerol and Saint-Émilion are left-bank appellations where Cabernet Sauvignon leads.
explanation: They are right bank, on limestone and clay, where Merlot leads.

stem: Condrieu is a Northern Rhône red made from Syrah.
explanation: Condrieu is white, mainly from Viognier.

stem: Champagne from the Vallée de la Marne is made mainly from Chardonnay.
explanation: Mainly Pinot Meunier. Chardonnay dominates the Côte des Blancs.
